sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a full cycle rather than a trend.

Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72], then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 to $44.0 billion [F6][D231] on higher shipment volumes and price realization [P43].
The peak was FY2023 at $61.3 billion [F8], and revenue has since fallen 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 to $45.7 billion [F10][D367][D412].
The FY2024 decline came from lower shipment volumes across both equipment segments, driven by rising grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates [P17].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver and the largest drag: 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], it fell 17.6% and subtracted 7.0pp from revenue growth [D658][D659].
U.S. and Canada sales volumes fell 30% in that segment, partly offset by a 22% volume increase in Brazil [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% and took 3.0pp off growth [D889][D890][D891], while Financial Services grew to 13.8% of revenue [D922].
Operating costs fell 7.3% against an 11.7% revenue decline, so operating costs fell 4.4pp less than revenue [D425][D412][D431].
EPS fell 27.8% in FY2025 against a 29.2% net income decline [D415][D413], as the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
The FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% [F30] sat above the 12.1% window median but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [D1335][D1334]; FY2025 operating income is not in the pack.
In FY2024 the margin fell 3.7pp [D378], with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D391][D390], as SG&A rose 5.3% on a 15.6% revenue decline [D381][D367].
In FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50] sat 2.7pp below FY2024's 13.7% [F49][D422], and the 20.1% effective tax rate [D400] left net margin 3.7pp under the FY2024 operating margin [D1373].
The margin cushion built in FY2021-FY2023 has largely unwound, and the FY2025 cost base is a smaller revenue base carrying fixed costs.
Operating cash flow of $7.46 billion was 1.48x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D401], above the 1.17x window median [D1364], and free cash flow of $6.10 billion was 1.21x net income [F100][D402].
The FY2025 inflow was driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Free cash flow margin of 13.4% [D398] was above the 11.6% window median [D1341], with capex at 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [D397][D403].
Cash conversion is the strongest part of the model, but the filing expects lower equipment operating cash flow in 2026 [P6].
Cash and equivalents were $8.28 billion at FY2025, up 13.0% [F140][D420], against $13.8 billion of current debt [X185].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021 [X191], so net cash and its peer rank cannot be computed across the window; the pack's net-cash figures stop at FY2021 [D226].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.86 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D409][D410], down from $8.64 billion and 121.9% in FY2023 [D319][D320], and the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
Return on average equity of 20.6% [D411] was below the 28.3% peer median [D1362], and net margin ranked in the 29th percentile of seven industrials peers [D1351].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025, from $61.3 billion to $45.7 billion [R1][F8][F10].
Two consecutive double-digit declines mark a cyclical downturn in the core agriculture business, not a one-year air pocket [R1].
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [R2][D657][D658], and Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% [R4][D889][D890].
The decline is broad rather than concentrated, which limits the offset any single segment can provide [R2][R4].
Long-term debt is missing after FY2021 and current debt missing before FY2020 [R9][R10][X191][X180], so net cash and debt growth are not comparable across the window.
Leverage conclusions rest on incomplete data, so the balance-sheet read is weaker than the cash-flow read [R9][R10].
Whether FY2026 revenue holds above the FY2025 level of $45.7 billion [F10], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether the operating margin recovers toward the 17.5% FY2024 level [F30] from the FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether free cash flow margin holds above the 11.6% window median [D1341] from 13.4% in FY2025 [D398], reported in the FY2026 10-K.
